properties.confidence_note: Declared national energy emergency March 2026; public reserve data available
properties.current_status: Declared national energy emergency. Suspended wholesale electricity spot market. Created emergency fuel-security fund. Implementing 4-day government work weeks.
properties.alternative_supply: Limited. No pipeline alternatives. Attempting emergency spot purchases. Domestic coal dominant but imported.
properties.rationing_capacity: Low. Limited state capacity to manage prolonged shortage. History of grid stress during typhoon season.
properties.one_line: 92% of oil from the Gulf, 45 days of reserves, energy emergency already declared.

properties.confidence_note: Active crisis well-documented; reserve data limited; LNG import data sparse
properties.current_status: Tightened fuel rationing. Reintroduced queuing systems. Four-day government work week. Emergency spot fuel purchases.
properties.alternative_supply: Minimal. Small domestic hydro base helps but insufficient. Emergency purchases at extreme premiums.
properties.rationing_capacity: Already rationing. Prior 2022 economic crisis built institutional muscle for austerity measures but population tolerance is low.
properties.one_line: Already rationing fuel with no public reserve data — Hormuz is an accelerant on existing fragility.

properties.confidence_note: Active crisis documented; reserve data unavailable; 99% of LNG from Qatar/UAE
properties.current_status: Fuel rationing imposed. Military deployed for anti-hoarding enforcement. Universities closed. Fertilizer plants temporarily shut. LNG costs forcing load-shedding.
properties.alternative_supply: Near zero. 99% of LNG from Qatar and UAE. No pipeline alternatives. Domestic gas production declining.
properties.rationing_capacity: Low. Military enforcement suggests political stress. History of grid instability and load-shedding even before crisis.
properties.one_line: 99% of LNG from Qatar/UAE, military deployed for fuel hoarding, universities shut — no reserve data public.

properties.confidence_note: Good reserve data; active government conservation measures documented
properties.current_status: Government-ordered energy conservation: bureaucrats required to take stairs, work from home. Considering oil-tax cuts. 95 days of reserves cited.
properties.alternative_supply: Limited. Some pipeline gas from Myanmar. Qatar supplies 28% of LNG (second-largest buyer). Exploring alternatives.
properties.rationing_capacity: Moderate. Government acting early with conservation measures. 95 days provides buffer but gas-heavy generation mix is the vulnerability.
properties.one_line: 95 days of reserves and active conservation measures, but 55% gas-fired generation is the structural exposure.

properties.confidence_note: Comprehensive data; 210 days strategic oil but only 9 days working LNG inventory
properties.current_status: National energy-saving campaign launched. President called for shorter showers and car restrictions. 70% of crude imports through Hormuz.
properties.alternative_supply: Some. Nuclear provides 18% baseload. Coal stockpiles exist. But working LNG terminal inventory is only ~9 days despite 210-day strategic oil reserve.
properties.rationing_capacity: High state capacity. Institutional ability to enforce conservation. The gap between 210-day oil reserves and 9-day LNG working stock is the real vulnerability.
properties.one_line: 210 days of strategic oil reserves but only 9 days of working LNG inventory — the mismatch is the risk.

properties.confidence_note: Generation mix clear; reserve data weak (20-45 days range); actively pursuing Russian alternatives
properties.current_status: Actively negotiating Russian oil and LNG deals. Seeking to diversify from Gulf dependence. Only 20-45 days of reserves. LNG under 2% of installed capacity.
properties.alternative_supply: Pursuing Russian alternatives. Domestic coal and hydro provide buffer. LNG dependency still small. Emergency procurement of 4M barrels non-Middle-Eastern oil (~6 days).
properties.rationing_capacity: Moderate. Coal and hydro provide structural resilience. The vulnerability is oil for transport and industry, not electricity generation.
properties.one_line: Coal and hydro provide a generation buffer, but 90% of oil is from the Gulf and reserves are thin at 20-45 days.

properties.stress_label: Price shock first, physical shortage later
properties.confidence_note: Extensive official data; reserve estimates vary (25-74 days); diversification actively underway
properties.current_status: Actively diversifying: 70% of oil rerouted to non-Hormuz sources. 90% of LPG imports still through Hormuz. Strategic reserves at 25-74 days depending on source.
properties.alternative_supply: Best positioned of the vulnerable countries. Coal-dominant generation reduces electricity exposure. Russian oil deals active. But 88% oil import dependent overall.
properties.rationing_capacity: High state capacity. Large domestic coal base insulates electricity. Primary risk is transport fuel and LPG for cooking, not grid collapse.
properties.one_line: Coal-dominant grid limits electricity exposure, but 88% oil import dependent and 90% of LPG through Hormuz.

properties.stress_label: Price shock first, physical shortage later
properties.confidence_note: Best data coverage of any country; 254-260 days of reserves; comprehensive IEA/EIA profiles
properties.current_status: Largest strategic reserves in Asia (257 days). 77% of seaborne oil from Middle East Gulf. Tokyo Electric has warned of potential rolling blackouts in extended scenario.
properties.alternative_supply: Best in Asia. Massive strategic reserves. Nuclear restart program. Diversified LNG sources. But volume dependency on Gulf crude is structurally high.
properties.rationing_capacity: Very high state capacity. Institutional experience from Fukushima energy conservation. Can sustain months of elevated prices before physical shortage.
properties.one_line: 257 days of reserves and strong state capacity — pain is price, not blackouts, unless disruption extends past 6 months.

properties.confidence_note: Excellent data; 245 days reserves (includes foreign-owned storage); 95% gas generation is the exposure
properties.current_status: No public emergency measures yet. As financial and refining hub, pain manifests as price before shortage. 45% of LNG from Qatar. Can buy time with money.
properties.alternative_supply: Large storage capacity (245 days, though much is foreign-owned). Refining hub status provides some flexibility. But 95% gas generation is extreme single-fuel exposure.
properties.rationing_capacity: Very high state capacity and fiscal reserves. Can subsidize and purchase at premium for extended period. The question is whether global LNG supply physically exists at any price.
properties.one_line: 95% gas generation and 45% of LNG from Qatar — money buys time, not immunity.

properties.confidence_note: Reserve data unavailable; conflicting reports on domestic vs import dependency; 99% of LNG from Gulf
properties.gen_mix_summary: Gas 25%, hydro 19%, coal 14%, nuclear 13%, renewables 13%, oil 10%
properties.current_status: Government claims 74% domestic power sources cushion LNG risk. Universities closed. Fertilizer plants shut. But LNG is 10% of generation and imported fuel critical for transport.
properties.alternative_supply: More diversified generation than it appears (hydro 19%, nuclear 13%). But 99% of LNG from Qatar/UAE. Domestic gas declining. No strategic reserve data public.
properties.rationing_capacity: Low. History of political instability and grid management challenges. Already experiencing rolling blackouts in many regions pre-crisis.
properties.one_line: Government says 74% domestic power sources, but 99% of LNG from Gulf, no public reserve data, universities already shut.

properties.confidence_note: Generation mix clear; reserve data essentially unavailable publicly; no crisis reporting yet
properties.current_status: No public emergency declarations. Decommissioned nuclear fleet (restarting planned). 70% of crude from Middle East. Reserve data not publicly available.
properties.alternative_supply: Limited. Decommissioned nuclear (restart planned). Coal stockpiles provide some buffer. But 42% gas generation with unclear LNG source diversification.
properties.rationing_capacity: High state capacity. But the absence of public reserve data is itself a signal — either reserves are thin or disclosure is politically sensitive.
properties.one_line: 85% fossil generation, no public reserve data, decommissioned nuclear — the data gap is the red flag.

properties.confidence_note: Grid collapse well-documented; not primarily Hormuz-driven; Venezuelan/US sanctions are the primary mechanism
properties.current_status: Repeated national grid collapses March 2026. Russia shipping fuel as humanitarian aid. US cut off Venezuelan oil supply to Cuba. Generation shortfall 1,300-1,700 MW during peak (half of demand).
properties.alternative_supply: Venezuelan supply cut by US policy. Russian humanitarian shipments. No market alternatives at scale. Decrepit domestic generation infrastructure.
properties.rationing_capacity: Already beyond rationing into collapse. Not a Hormuz case — this is blockade + infrastructure decay + loss of benefactor supply. Hormuz is an amplifier through global price pressure.
properties.one_line: Not a Hormuz case. Already inside the wreckage from US sanctions cutting Venezuelan oil. Hormuz amplifies via global prices.
